subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On a cold day, the body conserves heat by:
options: Vasodilation of skin arterioles
Relaxation of erector pili muscles
Increased sweating
Vasoconstriction of skin arterioles, reducing blood flow to the surface
questions.explain: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow near the skin surface, decreasing heat loss by radiation.

questions.q: During inspiration in a mammal, the pressure in the thorax falls because:
options: The diaphragm relaxes and domes upward
Surfactant reduces the surface tension of the alveoli
The volume of the thoracic cavity increases as the diaphragm flattens and the ribs move up and out
The external intercostal muscles relax
questions.explain: Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals increases thoracic volume, lowering pressure below atmospheric so air flows in.

questions.q: In the second messenger model of glucagon action, the binding of glucagon to its receptor leads to:
options: Activation of adenylate cyclase, raising cyclic AMP, which activates protein kinase A
Insulin being released by exocytosis
Direct entry of glucagon into the cell to activate enzymes
Opening of voltage-gated sodium channels
questions.explain: Glucagon activates adenylate cyclase, producing cAMP as a second messenger that activates protein kinase A to trigger glycogenolysis.

questions.q: In a pregnancy test, monoclonal antibodies are used to:
options: Bind specifically to the hCG hormone, giving a coloured line when present
Convert hCG into a dye
Produce hCG in the urine
Destroy the hCG hormone
questions.explain: Mobile antibodies bind hCG and are then trapped by immobilised antibodies in the test window, producing a visible coloured line.

questions.q: Ultrafiltration in the renal glomerulus occurs because:
options: Active transport pushes plasma into the Bowman's capsule
Plasma proteins are actively secreted into the filtrate
High hydrostatic blood pressure forces small molecules through the basement membrane, which acts as a filter
The afferent arteriole is wider than the efferent arteriole, lowering pressure
questions.explain: High pressure (helped by a narrower efferent arteriole) forces water and small solutes through the basement membrane, which holds back proteins and cells.

questions.q: During ventricular systole, the atrioventricular valves close because:
options: Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
Ventricular pressure exceeds atrial pressure
The ventricles are relaxing and filling
The semilunar valves are open
questions.explain: As the ventricles contract their pressure rises above that of the atria, forcing the AV valves shut to prevent backflow.

questions.q: Herd immunity protects unvaccinated individuals because:
options: The pathogen mutates to become harmless
A high proportion of immune people reduces the chance of an unvaccinated person meeting an infected person
Vaccines spread immunity through the air
Antibodies are passed between people on contact
questions.explain: When enough of the population is immune, transmission is interrupted, so susceptible individuals are unlikely to encounter the pathogen.

questions.q: The clonal selection and activation of a specific B-cell typically requires:
options: Antigen binding plus stimulation by an activated T-helper cell releasing cytokines
Phagocytosis of the B-cell
Only the antigen binding to the B-cell receptor
Binding to a memory cell
questions.explain: Most B-cells require both antigen binding and signals (cytokines) from T-helper cells to divide and differentiate.

questions.q: Why are antibiotics ineffective against viral infections such as HIV?
options: Antibiotics only work on fungi
Viruses have thicker cell walls
Viruses lack the metabolic processes and structures (e.g. cell walls, ribosomes) that antibiotics target
Viruses are too large to be affected
questions.explain: Antibiotics target bacterial structures and processes; viruses use host-cell machinery and lack these targets, so antibiotics do not affect them.

questions.q: Agglutination by antibodies helps destroy pathogens because:
options: It marks the antibody for destruction
It neutralises bacterial toxins by hydrolysis
Each antibody has two binding sites, so it clumps pathogens together, making them easier for phagocytes to engulf
It directly lyses the bacterial cell wall
questions.explain: With two binding sites an antibody can link several pathogens into clumps that phagocytes engulf more efficiently.

questions.q: Monoclonal antibodies are described as 'monoclonal' because they are:
options: Made only inside the human body
Identical antibodies produced from a single clone of cells, all specific to one antigen
A mixture of antibodies against several antigens
Produced by many different B-cells
questions.explain: They are derived from one B-cell clone, so every antibody is identical and binds the same specific antigen.

questions.q: During phagocytosis of a pathogen, the engulfed microbe is destroyed when:
options: Antibodies are released into the cytoplasm
The phagocyte divides by mitosis
Memory cells are produced directly
A phagosome fuses with a lysosome and lysozymes hydrolyse the pathogen
questions.explain: The pathogen is enclosed in a phagosome which fuses with a lysosome; lytic enzymes (lysozymes) then digest it.
